answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit work, then randomly audit a sample and slash deposits for provably false claims. Splitting one attacker into a thousand sybils does not multiply influence: each identity needs its own capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing it. An opal, zenith, or karst account earns no special trust; the attacker pays upfront and faces a measurable loss if caught.
